steps: Rinse the sabudana three times, cover with just enough water and soak until a pearl squashes easily between your fingers.
Tip it into a sieve and drain very well so no water is left at the bottom.
Dry roast the peanuts until crunchy, cool them and crush coarsely.
Mix the crushed peanuts, salt and sugar into the sabudana.
Boil the potato, peel it and cut into small cubes.
Heat the ghee, add the cumin, then the curry leaves, green chilli and grated ginger, and fry the potato for a minute.
Add the sabudana and stir on low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, until the pearls turn see-through.
Turn off the heat, add lemon juice and coriander, mix lightly and serve.
note: Sabudana is 65 g a plate, between the sources' 50 and 100 g, and the crushed peanuts keep the pearls from sticking. On a fasting day use rock salt and leave out the curry leaves if your family does.
